articles.title: Work on GEFS (the Good Enough File System) for OpenBSD progresses
articles.summary: A modern filesystem has been missing in OpenBSD for quite a while now. GEFS seems to fit the general mindset and is developed inside the tree already, so I’m really excited about it!

articles.title: Crunchy retro shooter Selaco Chapter 2 arrives November 13
articles.summary: The crunchy retro-shooter Selaco is about to get a massive content update with Selaco Chapter 2: The Machines of War releasing November 13th. Read the full article on GamingOnLinux .

articles.title: 3DO ODE Menu released
articles.summary: It works with Fixel’s FZ-1 ODE, XPort and with SataTo3DO-based clones: one menu for the common 3DO ODEs. There are some other clones out there that may or may not work, but I can add support for them when folks discover them.

articles.title: Always-on Apple Watch display showing the wrong time? Here’s the fix
articles.summary: Issues around daylight saving time switches date back to the Apple Watch Series 4 in 2018 . Apple applied a fix, but a similar problem emerged in 2021 and it has occurred again for some Apple Watch owners over the past week.

articles.title: iPhone Duo: Latest Buyer Wait Times
articles.summary: iPhone Duo order wait times averaged 89 days despite falling by a week, according to UBS Investment Bank data as of October 30. (Via Investing.com.) The USB Evidence Lab tracker covers iPhone availability across more than 30 markets, and puts the iPhone Duo buyer wait time at nearly three months, even after the slight improvement.

articles.title: Wear OS adding ‘system status bar’ to apps, Wear OS 7.1 coming
articles.summary: The upcoming feature in question is a “persistent system status bar over Wear OS app windows at the top position of the circular display.” It will display the “current time and system status indicators,” similar to Android on phones and tablets.

articles.title: OpenMW 0.52.0 for Morrowind gets a fresh release candidate to test new features
articles.summary: The amazing open source game engine OpenMW for the classic RPG Morrowind has released a release candidate for the upcoming 0.52.0 release. Lots of exciting changes are coming for players and modders, I've rounded-up some of the bigger bits along with the full changelog below.

articles.title: More Rules, Longer Lists? Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on a Hidden-Rule Curriculum
articles.summary: Self-evolving agents rewrite a persistent state from feedback, but it is largely untested whether this lets them learn a rule nobody told them. An agent can also pass by writing down each correction as an exception, and its list then grows with every new rule.

articles.title: DXVK-NVAPI 0.9.3 adds initial ARM64 support, DirectX Raytracing (DXR) upgrades
articles.summary: DXVK-NVAPI is the implementation of NVIDIA's NVAPI/NVOFAPI library for usage with DXVK and VKD3D-Proton - with a new release out now. Read the full article on GamingOnLinux .

articles.title: Beyond Plausible Prediction: Safety Sufficiency in Web World Models
articles.summary: Web world models increasingly predict the consequences of candidate actions before agents act, yet a plausible predicted future does not necessarily support the correct safety decision.

articles.title: SK Hynix expect the hardware crisis to continue through 2030
articles.summary: The company assessed that supply, on the other hand, is not keeping pace with the growth of the market. Given technical difficulty of leading-edge processes and the long lead time required to build new production facilities, it expects the structure in which demand exceeds supply to persist through 2030."

articles.title: Circumventing the Computational Hardness of Computational Arbitrage
articles.summary: AI model marketplaces host providers with heterogeneous costs and capabilities. These differences create an opportunity for computational arbitrage (Olmedo et al., 2026), in which an intermediary purchases inference from a portfolio of models and resells it to users at a profit.

articles.title: Incongruence-Aware Evaluation of Multimodal Speech Emotion Recognition in Audio Large Language Models
articles.summary: Voice-interactive large language models process both what a speaker says and how they say it, yet the two channels do not always agree. We ask whether that disagreement degrades speech emotion recognition.

articles.title: Cheap FPGA Board Becomes Retro-Style Computer
articles.summary: The Tang Nano 9K is a cheap FPGA development board that can usually be acquired for around $15 or so. [ThePartsBin] has been experimenting with this hardware and figured out how to set it up as a retro-style computer.

articles.title: Radeon RADV Vulkan Driver Adopts An LLM Policy
articles.summary: The Mesa RADV driver that provides Vulkan API support for AMD Radeon GPUs on Linux has adopted its own policy around AI / large language models (LLMs) for code contributions.

articles.title: Linux App Release Roundup (October 2026)
articles.summary: October’s Linux app releases brought plenty of treats, a couple of tricks and mercifully few frights. In this post, I recap the updates that landed last month.

articles.title: Enlightenment desktop 0.28 released with better networking
articles.summary: Enlightenment 0.28 has been released, the first major update to the open-source desktop environment since early 2025. Given the time between this and the previous 0.27 release, the changelog is suitably lengthy.
